Atomically replace all six disc slots on a build in one transaction.

build are stolen (re-attached here).

post.description:
Evaluate a team combo under Phase 5B — all members contribute damage.

The primary build (team slot 1) is the designated DPS. Steps without an
explicit ``agent_id`` are attributed to the primary build. Each team
member's snapshot is augmented with ``target=team`` modifiers from the
other members before the shared simulation runs.

Keystone endpoint (DESIGN_explainability.md §3.1).

Evaluates a team combo against a *specified* six-disc combination —
``disc_ids`` (persisted discs) or ``disc_stats`` (inline, for an
optimizer/rank candidate that isn't equipped) replace the equipped set
on the team member at ``active_index`` before stat resolution. Always
runs with full attribution via ``evaluate_combo_attributed`` (Task B1),
the same machinery ``/calculate`` uses — this is "run the calculator
with these six discs," never a second arithmetic path.

get.description:
Stat keys a custom (stage) buff may target — the stage-buff editor's picker.

Served rather than hardcoded client-side so the picker cannot drift from the buff
resolver's own vocabulary. That drift is the exact failure Task B2 exists to prevent:
a stat outside these buckets is accepted, displayed, and then silently ignored by the
calc, and a user whose numbers do not move has no way to tell "the buff did nothing"
from "the buff is not modelled". `docs/RESEARCH_custom_buff_stats.md` measured each
key end to end.

BuffContext.title: BuffContext
BuffContext.description:
User-toggled buff state for one calculation, sourced from the request only.

DESIGN_buff_context.md §2.1 — the server resolves buff state from the
request and only from the request; no endpoint reads
``build.active_conditions`` / ``build.stack_counts`` / ``build.disabled_buffs``
during a calculation. The three ``builds`` JSONB columns still exist and
still store data, but their role is now "defaults the client reads to
seed this object when a build loads" — never a fallback the server
consults mid-calculation.

``custom_buffs`` carries the stage/Deadly-Assault buffs of #64. They are synthesized
into ordinary ``Modifier`` rows in ``build_snapshot_from_db``, so nothing downstream
treats them as a special case (DESIGN_buff_context.md §2.3).

BuffPresetRead.title: BuffPresetRead
BuffPresetRead.description:
Response for buff-preset read endpoints.

``buffs`` is read back as :class:`StoredCustomBuff` — same shape, no vocabulary
checks. Writes go through :class:`CustomBuff` and are strict; reads must not be, or a
preset saved before a stat key was renamed would 500 the list endpoint and take the
whole panel down with it, including the user's ability to see and delete the preset
that did it. Applying a stale preset still fails loudly, at the calc request.

BuffPresetUpdate.title: BuffPresetUpdate
BuffPresetUpdate.description:
Body for ``PATCH /buff-presets/{id}`` — all fields optional, partial update.

``None`` here means "field absent", never "set this column to null": both columns are
``NOT NULL``. The route patches with ``exclude_unset=True``, so an omitted field is
already dropped — but an **explicit** ``{"name": null}`` survives that filter and
reached the DB as an IntegrityError, i.e. a 500 for what is plainly a bad request. The
validator below turns it into the 422 it always should have been.

BuffRosterEntrySchema.title: BuffRosterEntrySchema
BuffRosterEntrySchema.description:
One resolved buff, pivoted for a build-level "active buffs" panel.

Mirrors ``app.services.buff_roster.BuffRosterEntry``. Emitted once per
build (not per-step) alongside ``attribution``/``zone_formulas`` when
``with_attribution=true``. ``is_modeled=False`` marks a buff whose
``scaling_stat`` was never baked to a flat value — it is genuinely
active but contributes 0; shown rather than hidden (BRIEF_explainability.md).

CustomBuff.title: CustomBuff
CustomBuff.description:
One user-authored buff — a Deadly Assault / Shiyu stage buff, typically.

DESIGN_buff_context.md §2.3. A stage buff belongs to the *encounter* being
evaluated, not to a build, which is why it rides on the request-scoped
:class:`BuffContext` rather than on `builds`.

B3 synthesises these into ordinary ``Modifier`` rows (``source=EXTERNAL``,
``source_label=f"custom:{slug}"``), so condition gating, scope filtering, stacking,
attribution and ``disabled_buffs`` all work on them with no additional code. This
schema's whole job is to make sure nothing reaches that synthesis step that the calc
would then quietly drop.

Every field is validated against the engine's own vocabulary, and an unknown value is
a 422 rather than a silently skipped buff: a user who authors a stage buff and sees
their numbers not move has no way to tell "the buff did nothing" from "the buff is
not modelled".

When set, each build's EX-Special damage is credited by an energy-feasibility factor derived from its ER (base + disc) over rotation_duration_s, so ER% influences rankings. null (default) credits EX damage in full (current behavior).

rotation_duration_s.title: Rotation Duration S
rotation_duration_s.description: Wall-clock seconds over which passive energy regen accrues; only used when rotation_energy_cost is set.

fluxed_element.title: Fluxed Element
fluxed_element.description: Attribute Flux override, Lumiflux agents only (e.g. Remielle). When set, this element's `<element>_dmg` disc stat is unioned into the top-K prefilter keep-set instead of the auto-derived value (the element of the next team slot, cyclic). With no team_id, a solo/empty team, or a non-Lumiflux agent, the derived value is null: no attribute DMG% disc stat is unioned (a Lumiflux agent has no such bucket by design). A missing team is therefore the documented default, not a calc bug.

EvaluateDiscsRequest.title: EvaluateDiscsRequest
EvaluateDiscsRequest.description:
Evaluate a team combo against a specified six-disc combination (DESIGN §3.1).

The keystone endpoint: swaps ``disc_ids`` (persisted discs) or
``disc_stats`` (inline stats, e.g. an unpersisted optimizer candidate)
onto the team member at ``active_index`` before stat resolution, then
evaluates with full attribution. Exactly one of ``disc_ids``/``disc_stats``
must be set.

HitMode.title: HitMode
HitMode.description:
How an `Attack`'s hits group for damage calc: single, cycling, context-variant, or held.

The last three are *parameterized* modes — a combo step carries one value that decides
how the move's rows resolve (`cycle_position`, `variant_label`, `channel_s` respectively).
CHANNEL differs from the other two in kind: its parameter is a quantity, not a row
selector, so it scales the `tick`-role rows rather than picking among them
(docs/DESIGN_channeled_moves.md §4.1).

StoredCustomBuff.title: StoredCustomBuff
StoredCustomBuff.description:
The *shape* of a custom buff, with none of the vocabulary checks.

Read model only, for data already sitting in a `buff_presets` row (#64). The
vocabulary a stage buff draws on — `CUSTOM_BUFF_STATS`, `Condition`, `AttackScope` —
is the engine's, and the engine's changes: a stat key gets renamed and every preset
saved against the old name becomes unvalidatable. Validating on *read* would then turn
a stale saved row into a 500 on `GET /buff-presets`, breaking the panel for that user
with no way back — they cannot even see the offending preset to delete it.

So the strictness is placed where it belongs: **strict on write** (`CustomBuff`, where
the user is authoring and can fix it), **permissive on read** (here), **loud on use**
(applying a stale preset copies its buffs into a request, which 422s naming the stat).
A stale preset stays visible, deletable and honest about what it holds.

disabled_buffs.description: Buffs to exclude from this calc, as buff_id() values or a stage buff's 'custom:<slug>' (DESIGN_buff_context.md §2.1). Replaces each member's disabled_buffs column entirely -- never merged with it. Without this field the keystone endpoints applied a buff the run that produced the candidate had switched off, so clicking a candidate showed a number that run could not reproduce.

fluxed_element.title: Fluxed Element
fluxed_element.description: Attribute Flux override, Lumiflux agents only (e.g. Remielle). When set, this element is used for DMG%-bucket selection and enemy-RES targeting instead of the auto-derived value (the element of the next team slot, cyclic). With no team (solo calc), a solo/empty team, or a non-Lumiflux agent, the derived value is null and the agent deals pure Lumiflux damage: no attribute DMG% bonus applies and the enemy RES contribution is a neutral 0. A missing team is therefore the documented default, not a calc bug.
